Definition: from a compound of G5469 and the reduplicated form of G71; to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively):--bridle.
BiblicalUsage: Chalinagogeo means to bridle, to hold with a bit. James says the man who seems religious but bridles not his tongue deceives his own heart, and the man who offends not in word is able also to bridle the whole body.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the tongue is the horse and the bridle is the test: hold the tongue, and the whole body follows.
